sentences.text: Patagonykus puertai is the sole species of this extinct alvarezsauroid theropod, a group of dinosaurs that lived roughly 92 million years ago in South America.

The holotype, defined as the specific specimen used to describe the species, contains a well-preserved skeleton missing the skull but retaining many vertebrae, shoulder bones, a partial arm, hip bones, and legs.
This animal featured powerful hind legs and reduced front limbs that ended in a single claw.
Scientists estimate the creature could grow up to two meters long and weigh approximately 47 kilograms.
It is believed that Patagonykus may have been covered in feathers.
The genus was discovered in the Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén Basin in Neuquén Province.
The genus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae, which also includes Mononykus and Alvarezsaurus.
Within the broader superfamily Alvarezsauroidea, Patagonykus is specifically placed as the sister genus to Bonapartenykus in the subgroup Patagonykinae.
This dinosaur lived from the Turonian to the Coniacian stages, between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago.
